analysis: What changed versus the 6:00 AM brief: the split tape survived the open — Nasdaq +1.28%, S&P 500 +0.38%, Dow -474 (-0.92%) — and the chip bounce strengthened into regular trading rather than fading. Nvidia is now +7.05% (vs +4.53% premarket), AMD +13.44% (vs +7.1%) and Micron +9.48% (vs +7.8%): the leaders are retracing roughly half of Thursday's losses in the session, not just in thin premarket volume. Moderna flipped outright, from about -2% premarket to +8.02% in the session — the beat-and-raise finally found buyers. DraftKings worsened to -27.55%. The hot payrolls print (+165K vs 59K expected) repriced December hike odds to 78% from 70%, and the tape took it in stride. Tesla extended its Cybertruck-pivot gains to +3.71%. Signal vs noise: the breadth of the chip bounce in regular trading, the VIX compressing to 26.70 from Thursday's 28.18 close, and the Moderna reversal are signal; the Dow's continued slide is rotation out of defensives that held up Thursday, not broad panic; the recirculated Apple iPhone order-cut story is noise until confirmed — the 6 AM brief flagged it as a month-old report. The community reads the bounce as fragile: WSB's dominant view is a small bounce Friday, another dump Monday, and HN's correction thread is debating bottom vs dead-cat bounce.

headlines.headline: The split tape held through the open: the Nasdaq Composite rose 1.28%, the S&P 500 was up 0.38%, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 474 points, or 0.92%, in the first minutes of the regular session.
headlines.why_it_matters: The Nasdaq-led bounce survived the open but the Dow keeps sliding — rotation out of Thursday's defensive winners, not a broad rally.

headlines.headline: Chips extended the premarket bounce into the session: Nvidia +7.05% to $194.40 (prior close $181.60), AMD +13.44% to $458.74 (prior close $404.40) and Micron +9.48% to $718.60 (prior close $656.39) in early trading.
headlines.why_it_matters: The leaders are retracing roughly half of Thursday's losses in regular trading, not just thin premarket volume — the bounce now has sponsorship, at least for now.

headlines.headline: Moderna flipped from a premarket fade to +8.02% at $260.83 in early trading after its Q3 beat-and-raise — revenue $1.313B vs ~$885M consensus, EPS $0.38 vs an expected $1.25 loss — and raised full-year revenue growth guidance to 15-25%.
headlines.why_it_matters: A beat-and-raise that was fading premarket is now being bought in the session — buyers are selective, but they are showing up for genuine earnings strength.

headlines.headline: DraftKings cratered further to -27.55% at $17.04 (prior close $23.52) in early trading after slashing guidance to fund a spending push.
headlines.why_it_matters: Guidance cuts still get punished hard and the selling deepened after the open — the mirror of Moderna, where a raised outlook is being paid.

headlines.headline: Tesla rose 3.71% to $356.46 in early trading, extending its gains on the plan to wind down Cybertruck production around mid-2027 and shift Giga Texas capacity to Cybercab.
headlines.why_it_matters: The market keeps reading the Cybertruck wind-down as focus on the robotaxi bet rather than failure — the gain held and grew past the open.

headlines.headline: December Fed hike odds repriced to 78% after the hot October payrolls print (+165,000 jobs vs 59,000 expected, unemployment 4.1%), up from a 70% chance before the release, per Reuters.
headlines.why_it_matters: Hot jobs keep a December hike firmly live, yet the tape took the repricing in stride — growth strength, not a rate shock, is the market's read so far.

headlines.headline: Megacaps split at the open: Meta +2.35% to $619.31, Alphabet +1.99% to $288.20 and Amazon +1.10% to $263.06, while Microsoft fell 0.88% to $531.21 and Apple slipped 0.40% to $342.81, still the laggard. Apple is lower as a report that it cut component orders for the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max on weaker demand recirculates.
headlines.why_it_matters: Apple keeps lagging the bounce and Microsoft joined it lower, so the megacap recovery is uneven. The order-cut report is single-source and the same story the 6 AM brief flagged as a month old — treat as fragile until confirmed.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC news overnight. The $0.525 per-unit distribution pays TODAY, Friday Nov 6, to holders of record Oct 26. The Nov 3 Q3 story carries forward: record revenue $357.2M (+43% year over year, vs ~$348.32M consensus), record Adjusted EBITDA $197.3M, DCF coverage 1.67x, EPS $0.33 vs $0.3345 expected, distribution held at $0.525, full-year guidance tightened to Adjusted EBITDA $770-780M and DCF $495-505M. On the call, management said over 60% of 2027 horsepower deliveries are contracted (about 90% of first-half deliveries), but flagged cost pressure: monthly lubricant costs exited Q3 about 25% above first-half levels and diesel hit an all-time high in September, with pricing not yet fully reflecting the increases.
